newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU finance ministers begin meeting on budget pact.
newsitem.headline: EU finance ministers begin meeting on budget pact.

text.p: European Union finance ministers began meeting on Thursday to resolve outstanding issues over a budget accord that keeps deficits under control among countries joining a common currency.

The German-inspired stability pact has been one of the most contentious issues in the runup to a single currency, with sharp differences over a strict definition of a recession seen as the main stumbling block.
The budgetary mechanism, designed to keep deficits under three percent of gross domestic product, would include fines of up to 0.5 percent of total output.
But a precise defintion over the extent of an economic downturn which would let countries avoid fines has remained elusive. Germany argued initially for a definition of a 2.0 percent decline in GDP.
Others want a range of growth, between a fall of 0.5 and 2.0 percent of GDP.
Arriving for the meeting, ministers were mixed in their assessment of whether a deal could be struck this evening, ahead of a summit of EU leaders on Friday and Saturday.
